messages:
sam: Hey team — ran into two annoying redwoodctl DX issues on Ubuntu CI and in tmux. apt-installed binary ended up in /snap/bin and my CI image PATH doesn’t include it, so `redwoodctl login` fails. Also when I run inside tmux the device-code flow tries to open a browser but nothing happens (no $DISPLAY). Anyone seen this?

jasper: Yup. For CI we just symlink to /usr/local/bin in the Dockerfile: `ln -s $(which redwoodctl) /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl` — quick and dirty.

maria: If it’s the snap package, which prints `/snap/bin/redwoodctl`. You can add `/snap/bin` to PATH in the CI image or avoid snap and use the curl install script. Adding snap to PATH feels gross for containers.

leo: For tmux/headless you can use the headless flow: `redwoodctl login --headless`. It prints a code + URL you can use from another machine/browser. That worked for me when I couldn’t open a browser.

sam: Good call, `--headless` fixed the tmux hang. But another thing: localserve created a duplicate profile for me — I had `dev` and now there’s `dev (1)`. Did localserve create a temp profile and fail to clean up?

jasper: :facepalm: We’ve seen profile name collisions when localserve writes a temp profile and cleanup fails on container exit. Pinging devops-bot to capture logs.

devops-bot: devops-bot: Observed failed cleanup on container exit in 0.12.3. Filing ticket RDW-1234. Workaround: `redwoodctl profile remove \"dev (1)\"` after stopping localserve.

maria: Can the installer prefer `~/.local/bin` when `/usr/local/bin` isn’t writable? Many CI and restricted nodes don’t allow writing to /usr/local.

sam: Also, in non-interactive shells redwoodctl currently prints the browser prompt and then hangs waiting for a TTY. It should detect non-TTY and default to headless.

jasper: Agreed. Small PR idea: if stdout/stderr is not a TTY, auto-switch to headless and log something like `Detected non-interactive shell: defaulting to --headless`.

leo: I also hit flaky token cache permissions when running under podman rootless. The token file ended up owned by root in some packagers. Might be umask or packager step.

sam: TL;DR workarounds collected: 1) symlink to /usr/local/bin or add /snap/bin to PATH in CI, 2) use `redwoodctl login --headless` in tmux/CI, 3) remove duplicate profiles with `redwoodctl profile remove`, 4) if token files are root-owned, check packager umask. I’ll open an issue with repro steps and logs.

maria: :thumbsup: Can someone paste the Dockerfile snippet for the symlink? I’ll add it to docs.

jasper: Dockerfile snippet:
```
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y ca-certificates 
RUN curl -sSL https://install.redwood.ai/redwoodctl.sh | sh
RUN ln -s /snap/bin/redwoodctl /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl || true
```
We should make the installer detect /snap/bin and fallback to ~/.local/bin when /usr/local is not writable.

sam: Thanks. Filing issue with logs. Quick tmux debug I used: `TERM=screen-256color tmux new -d \"redwoodctl login\" ; sleep 2 ; tmux capture-pane -p -S -100` — shows the browser prompt but nothing opens.

ci-bot: ci-bot: Build job #4527 failed on ubuntu-20.04: PATH did not include /snap/bin; install step succeeded but runner couldn't execute redwoodctl.

devops-bot: RDW-1234 created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RDW-1234 — maintainer assigned.

maria: Nice. I added a checklist item to onboarding docs: verify redwoodctl ends up in PATH for CI/container images and document headless login flow.

sam: Thanks all, will post the issue link and paste the tmux capture output there.
